messages.subject: FIML and Multiple Imputation
parts:
Dear all,
I am new to lavaan and first I would like to thank you for this great work. A user-friendly sem package like lavaan with a focus on offering a large choice of features (estimators, fit measures etc) was much needed in R ! I have two questions:
1/ FIML: in Mplus, it seems that FIML can be used when dependent variables are missing (e.g. successive measurments in a growth model) but also when predictors are missing. I am not sure if this is possible in lavaan and, if so, how to do it.
2/ If I read correctly, multiple imputation is not yet available on lavaan. As you know, there are other packages to generate imputed data sets (mice or amelia) and some other packages to combine estimates (mice or zelig). I like the implementation in zelig because the user only need to pass the argument data=ImputedData, instead of data = Data (were imputedData is a list of imputed data sets generated in an other package).
Maybe building on the existing packages or code would enable an easier implementation of multiple imputation in lavaan?
Many Thanks
JB

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: FIML and Multiple Imputation
parts:
On 03/14/2013 11:48 PM, JB wrote:
> Dear all,
> I am new to lavaan and first I would like to thank you for this great
> work. A user-friendly sem package like lavaan with a focus on offering a
> large choice of features (estimators, fit measures etc) was much needed
> in R ! I have two questions:
> 1/ FIML: in Mplus, it seems that FIML can be used when dependent
> variables are missing (e.g. successive measurments in a growth model)
> but also when predictors are missing. I am not sure if this is possible
> in lavaan and, if so, how to do it.

I believe that Mplus will remove all cases with missing values on
exogenous (independent) variables by default. If you specify
missing="ml" in lavaan, lavaan switches to FIML, but currently (0.5)
regards *all* variables (including the exogenous variables) as random,
and hence will not throw away any cases. Which may or may not be what
you want.

> 2/ If I read correctly, multiple imputation is not yet available on
> lavaan.

Have a look a the semTools package. It includes a function 'runMI()'
doing exactly what you propose.

Yves.

messages.author: 84e6ff87e445f88b
messages.subject: Re: FIML and Multiple Imputation
parts:
Dear Yves,
Thanks for your answer. Yes, keeping the cases with missing data on exogenous variables was what I wanted.
And the runMI function in semTools is also exactly what I wanted, and very flexible (I can feed my own imputed data sets).
Thanks again for your work!
JB
